title: The people close
hookLine: the story was never only ten men; it was a whole sangat

lines: THE EYE GOES TO THE CENTER.
THE EDGES ARE FULL OF PEOPLE.
cards: A painting of a Guru's court. The Guru sits at the center, under a canopy, and that's where the eye goes first. But stay with it a moment longer.
At the edges are other figures. Someone waving the chaur. A musician with an instrument.
A woman at the side. A man carrying water. An old man with a white beard.
A visitor in a Sufi's cap. Each figure was painted by someone who thought they belonged in the picture. The center only makes sense because of the edges.

teach.b: Lately we've been looking at the edges of the painting. Start with family. Mata Tripta and Mehta Kalu, with their love and worry.
Bebe Nanaki, the sister who stood by her brother. Mata Sulakhni, steady at home. Mata Khivi, with her generous kitchen.
Bibi Amro, whose song changed a life. Bibi Bhani, who held the stool steady. Mata Ganga, Mata Nanaki, Bibi Viro, Mata Gujri.
Mata Jito, Mata Sundari, Mata Sahib Kaur.
Then the servants and companions. Baba Buddha, who served Guru after Guru. Bhai Gurdas, who was tested too.
Bhai Bidhi Chand, a thief turned true. Kirpa Ram, who came back to serve. Daya Singh and the rest of the five, the Panj Pyare.
Sangat Singh, who took the Guru's place. Moti Ram Mehra with warm milk. Mai Bhago, who led them back.
Bhai Mani Singh, the steady scribe. Bhai Jaita, called the Guru's own son.
And the friends: Mian Mir, Budhu Shah, Nabi Khan and Ghani Khan, the Nawab of Malerkotla, Todar Mal, Rai Kalha. And the far-off sangats waiting for letters. Gurbani has a word for this.
Sangat, the company, and sat sangat, the true company.
Guru Nanak asks, on Ang 72, how the true company is known, and answers: it's where the one Name is praised. That's a paraphrase. The Gurus' story was never ten men alone on a stage.
It was a gathering, and the gathering is part of the teaching. Next, the path turns to a hard stretch for the Khalsa, and it begins at Nanded, with an ascetic who will become a servant.

how: Sikhs remember the family, companions and friends of the Gurus in kirtan, in katha and in the stories told at gurdwaras, and the sangat, the gathered community, is central to Sikh worship.

o: the true company, gathered where the Name is praised
a gathering of the Gurus' own family members only
a holy place where Sikhs go on pilgrimage

games.q: the people close — tap the pairs.

s: the Gurus' story is the story of ten men alone
it was a whole sangat: family, servants, companions and friends.
Guru Nanak says the true company is known where the one Name is praised
the people close to the Gurus were all men
Bebe Nanaki, Mata Khivi, Bibi Bhani, Mai Bhago and other women stand in the story too.

games.q: you're painting a Guru's court and you're short on space. what do you do?
o: paint only the Guru, large, at the center.
keep the Guru at the center and fill the edges with his people.
games.why: the story itself does this: the center makes sense because the edges are full of people.

practice: Picture your own life as a painting and look to the edges: family who worried for you, friends who stood close, someone of another faith who opened a door, someone far away who still writes.
Name them silently, one at a time, and give each name one breath.

wordCard.voice: sat sangat, the true company. Guru Nanak says on Ang 72 that it's where the one Name is praised; the family, servants, companions and friends around the Gurus are part of it. Today's word.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: satsangat, the true company, as Guru Nanak uses it on Ang 72.

carryVoice: Your line: a whole sangat. Nobody in this story stands alone. Eight hundred thirty-six days, and counting.
